articles.title: Trump admin cracks 'garbage' joke after fatal blizzard it wouldn't help blue states fight
articles.description: President Donald Trump's officials at the Federal Emergency Management Agency cracked mean jokes Wednesday about a deadly blizzard to which they were refused to commit resources. The comment appeared in a new Politico report on White House officials who overrode FEMA experts and refused to approve disaster relief for states that voted against Trump in the presidential election. The blizzard in question took place earlier this year, causing deaths and affecting New York, New Jersey, Massachusetts, and Rhode Island. Email chains reviewed by Politico confirm that agency officials had already determined New York met the criteria for disaster relief. According to the report, "snow assistance was targeted for elimination last year in a memo by FEMA leadership as a way to reduce spending. Congress pushed back on that idea — a signal the administration may have disregarded." Since 1999, 82 percent of snow assistance from FEMA has gone to states controlled by the Democratic Party — a disparity caused by the fact that Democrats tend to be stronger in northern states with colder climates. When an agency spokesperson was confronted about the denials by Politico, they responded with a disparaging joke. “If the federal government is paying for regular operations like snow removal, what next? Garbage removal?” said the spokesperson. “The federal government’s role is not to fund routine functions.” Under the Trump administration, FEMA has been involved in other controversies as well, including reports that their resources are being diverted to "pre-crime" enforcement against terrorism, and a senior official who was ousted after claiming God teleported him to a Waffle House .

articles.title: Horoscope for Wednesday, July 29, 2026
articles.description:
Moon Alert

There are no restrictions to shopping or important decisions today. The Full Moon peaks in Aquarius at 9:36 a.m.

Aries (March 21-April 19)

A positive day

Today you might feel tension with romantic partners. Because of the full moon energy, you might also feel at odds with a friend, a member of a group, or even your kids. This will pass in about a day or so. Don't get your belly in a rash.

Taurus (April 20-May 20)

An average day

Today you might be pulled between the demands of home and family versus the demands of your career, your job or your responsibilities to society. This is because of the full moon. Each full moon is different, and this one encourages your focus on home and family.

Gemini (May 21-June 20)

A positive day

Pay attention to everything you say and do because this is a mildly accident-prone day due to the full moon. Take a moment before you act or say something that you might later regret. Be aware of your surroundings.

Cancer (June 21-July 22)

An average day

You're never casual about money, and today is no exception. The full moon might create confusion, tension or disputes between your wealth versus what somebody else claims or wants. This includes debt and discussions about inheritances. Stay chill.

Leo (July 23-Aug. 22)

A positive day

Today, the only full moon opposite your sign all year is taking place, which could create tension between you and those who are closest to you, especially spouses, partners and dear friends. Don’t make a big deal about anything. This tension is gone in 24 hours.

Virgo (Aug. 23-Sept. 22)

An average day

Be patient with co-workers today. Likewise, be patient with people who might be involved in health procedures. You might need more patience than usual dealing with a pet. That's because these are the areas that could feel stressed by today's full moon.

Libra (Sept. 23-Oct. 22)

A positive day

This is a dicey day for social occasions, the arts, friendships and especially romance. (It can also be stressful for parents dealing with their kids.) On the upside, you might see things that you never realized before. You might have increased clarity about something, especially a relationship. However, feelings could be running high.

Scorpio (Oct. 23-Nov. 21)

An average day

Today you might feel like you're caught in a tug-of-war between trying to please the demands of home and family and dealing with your career and your outer world. You can't please both. For this particular full moon, you can't ignore your career and your responsibilities to society.

Sagittarius (Nov. 22-Dec. 21)

A positive day

The energy of today's full moon can introduce an accident-prone influence for your sign. This means be mindful and alert. Pay attention to everything you say and do. Slow down and keep your eyes open. This applies to driving, jogging, walking and talking!

Capricorn (Dec. 22-Jan. 19)

An average day

Financial issues might come to a head today. This might concern your debt, how you're handling your money, or taking care of your possessions. It might also relate to shared property or something that someone else owns. It is what it is.

Aquarius (Jan. 20-Feb. 18)

An average day

Today the full moon is in your sign, which is why you might feel tension dealing with those who are closest to you. Something you've been working on might be completed. Certainly, your feelings are heightened and your focus on partners and close friends is stronger.

Pisces (Feb. 19-March 20)

A positive day

Relations with co-workers might be strained today because of the energy of the full moon. However, it's also possible that you will have wrapped up some old business and you feel good about it. Meanwhile, increased chaos and busyness at home continue.

If today is your birthday

Business magnate, investor, philanthropist Li Ka-shing (1928) shares your birthday today. You are positive, energetic and will work tirelessly to achieve success. You're protective and influential. This is a year of new beginnings, adventures, and major changes. What you do now will bring great benefits in the future. Prepare for leadership. Take action and define your goals.

articles.title: Birdwatch: A song thrush connects me with the great-grandfather I never knew
articles.description: No other bird speaks to us quite so directly, its serenade conjuring memories of old family tales I wake early on these bright summer mornings. And now that the birds in my garden have mostly fallen silent, only one is still serenading me at this hour: the aptly named song thrush. Its measured, deliberate repetitions – which this particular bird has provided without a break since the turn of the year – are unmistakable. Whenever I hear a song thrush, I’m taken back in time. First, to my childhood, when the first sign of spring was when thrushes started singing from the roofs of our suburban housing estate as I walked home from school in the dim light of a February afternoon. Continue reading...

articles.title: Ships stuck in strait of Hormuz pose ‘super-spreader’ biodiversity threat, scientists warn
articles.description: Biologists say cargo ships stranded in Gulf may carry highly potent invasive species around the world as trade resumes The closure of the strait of Hormuz has created conditions for an extreme global biodiversity threat, with scientists warning that thousands of stranded ships could spread invasive marine species across the world’s oceans once they begin sailing again. More than 1,500 commercial vessels have been stuck in the Gulf since the strategic waterway closed on 28 February after the outbreak of the US-Israel war on Iran . An international team of marine biologists said that with the stranded ships remaining motionless, their hulls were becoming encrusted with marine life – from microbes and algae to barnacles and other invertebrates – that could hitchhike to ports around the world when trade resumed.
